med_findings.title: An ActiveJob reserved key inside the utm_data jsonb makes PosthogTrackJob.perform_later raise ActiveJob::SerializationError inside the fan-out
confirmed_by: agent 8 (both webhook writers, plus the organization.utm_data column)
agent 9 (independent reproduction on a different org)
consequences_observed: trial_started path: the raise escapes Organization#update! to its caller; the ledger row persists; Discord::NotifyFreeTrialStartedJob is lost; PostHog event is lost
trial_started path: organization_ai_credit_balance&.reset_ai_credits is SKIPPED (A9-M1 — the writer call occupies the line the removed Discord enqueue held, ahead of reset_ai_credits)
both webhook writers: the insertion's own rescue swallows it — ledger row persists while the PostHog event and the Discord cash notification are silently lost; nothing escapes handle_stripe_event
reachable via either side of the owner-first fallback (users.utm_data or organizations.utm_data)
med_findings.orchestrator_reasoning: MED on reachability, not on fix cost. The QA HIGH bar is wrong behavior 'during any reasonable workflow'; the app's own frontend cannot produce the trigger (app/javascript/shared/lib/utils.js:192-208 filters utm_data keys to the utm_ prefix, and all five ActiveJob reserved keys begin with _aj_, so they cannot survive that filter). It takes a hand-crafted POST to the public signup endpoint (registrations_controller.rb:328 permits utm_data: {} with no key restriction) carrying a deliberately chosen ActiveJob-reserved key — adversarial input, not an accidental workflow. The code is also exactly spec-compliant: D9 and SPEC §7 name utm_data in the 13 attribution fields, owner-first via attribution_value, .compact. This is a defect in the approved design, not a deviation from it, so 'spec-implementation mismatch is never MED' does not apply; two MED criteria apply squarely (spec-compliant-but-imperfect, requires a design decision).
med_findings.verified_not_a_pre_existing_pattern: All 11 other PosthogTrackJob callers pass hand-built scalar hashes (magic_links_controller.rb:24, auth/invites_controller.rb:50,80, billing_controller.rb:115,213,311, sessions_controller.rb:11, registrations_controller.rb:52,208, omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb:47, email_processor.rb:83). subscription_event.rb:59 is the only site in the codebase passing user-controlled data to perform_later, so the 'consistent with existing patterns' MED criterion does NOT apply and the exposure is feature-introduced.
med_findings.blast_radius_pinned_by_orchestrator: The nil -> 'trialing' flip happens inside Organization#sync_with_stripe, called from stripe_webhook_handler_job.rb:161,205,237 and billing_controller.rb:171,211,260,624. An unrescued raise on the controller path could 500 a user's checkout-return request.
fix_options_for_owner: rescue around enqueue_posthog_track in subscription_event.rb — feature-local, no spec deviation, but makes PostHog failures silent (agent 7's proposal)
drop utm_data from the payload — contradicts D9's explicit field list
JSON-stringify utm_data — changes the wire shape D9 approved
restrict the utm_data: {} permit at registrations_controller.rb:328 — edits a file SPEC §2 lists as explicitly untouched, and is a pre-existing permissiveness
do nothing — accept it as adversarial-input-only
med_findings.action_taken: None. No fix agent dispatched: selecting among these is Jessica's design decision, and a unilateral pick is the failure pattern pipeline rules 10, 20 and 23 exist to prevent.

subscription_events.amount is a 4-byte integer; an amount_paid above 2147483647 loses the conversion row inside the ledger block's own rescue. Requires a >$21.4M single invoice — not reachable.

The partial unique index does not constrain NULL stripe_subscription_id. Proven unreachable from both webhook insertions: Stripe::Subscription.retrieve(nil) raises locally before HTTP, so the main-plan branch is never entered.
conversion_duplicate_exists? queries globally rather than org-scoped; verified live with two real orgs. Outcome is SPEC §3's stated invariant (Stripe subscription ids are globally unique).
Repeat trial_started is possible beyond the 5-minute dedupe, but no production path returns stripe_subscription_status to nil.
A late invoice for a superseded subscription stamps the org's current plan — exactly what SPEC §5.2 specifies.
